To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Clostridium difficle TcdB induces cell death with pyknotic nuclei and nuclear blistering.

Clostridium difficle toxin B induces two different and apparently independent effects: (1) cell rounding due glucosylation of the Rho GTPase Rac, and (2) shrinkage of the cells and blistering of the nucleus due to the high concentrations of the toxin.
TcdB induces pyknotic death which is independent of the glucosylation activity.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the pathogenesis of C. difficile.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of TcdA and its homologue TcdB.
the cytotoxic effects of Clostridum difficile toxin B.
